candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
candidate.educational_objective: Relate hypochloremia to prolonged vomiting and interpret chloride within fluid/electrolyte and acid-base context.

options.A: Prolonged vomiting can contribute to decreased serum chloride and the result should be interpreted with the client's fluid and acid-base status
options.B: Low chloride proves a single kidney diagnosis without considering the clinical context
options.C: Low chloride is unrelated to fluid, electrolyte, or acid-base balance
options.D: Prolonged vomiting is expected to raise chloride above the reference interval

candidate.rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories describes serum chloride as useful for evaluating water, electrolyte, and acid-base status and lists persistent gastric secretion and prolonged vomiting among causes of decreased chloride. Chloride should therefore be interpreted in the broader clinical and electrolyte context rather than as a disease-specific marker.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports chloride testing for fluid/electrolyte/acid-base status and decreased chloride with prolonged vomiting.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Information; adult reference interval and causes of decreased chloride
candidate.stem: An adult has a serum chloride level below the laboratory reference interval and has had prolonged vomiting. How should the nurse interpret the result?
